expected.rationale: All three frozen outcomes are answered, including completed-turn timing. The lifecycle passage describes the shared agent scoring worker before its RemoteScorer-specific steps; the candidate does not generalize HTTP endpoint behavior to all Signals. Expect every outcome answered and a passed normal-release verdict.

claims.text: Tracing captures agent activity; evaluations test behavior on chosen examples; Signals score traced agent turns after they finish.
claims.answer_quote: Tracing captures the agent activity; evaluations test behavior on chosen examples; Signals score traced agent turns after they finish [S3][S2][S8].
claims.scope_reason: Each part matches its page: S3 for tracing, S2 for evaluations, S8 for completed-turn scoring.

claims.text: The Agents SDK records conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool executions; each emits an OpenTelemetry span; traces appear as nested activity in the Agents tab.
claims.answer_quote: The Agents SDK records conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool executions. Each operation emits an OpenTelemetry span, and the traces appear as nested activity in the Agents tab [S3].
claims.scope_reason: S3 documents the Weave SDK for Agents and its tracing model.

claims.text: An Evaluation defines a dataset or list of examples and scoring functions; calling .evaluate() runs it against a model or function and produces an evaluation run, for measuring behavior on repeatable examples and comparing changes.
claims.answer_quote: An `Evaluation` defines a dataset or list of examples and scoring functions. Calling `.evaluate()` runs it against a model or function and produces an evaluation run, so you can measure behavior on repeatable examples and compare changes [S2].
claims.scope_reason: S2 covers this in the Python and TypeScript descriptions.

claims.text: When a root span ends, Weave treats it as a completed turn and emits weave.genai.turn_ended; the scoring worker loads active Signals targeting that event and applies their filters and sampling rates. Tags and ratings appear on the Signals tab.
claims.answer_quote: When a root span ends, Weave treats it as a completed turn and emits `weave.genai.turn_ended`; the scoring worker then loads active Signals targeting that event and applies their filters and sampling rates. Tags and ratings appear on the Signals tab [S8][S1].
claims.scope_reason: S8 steps 1, 2 and 4 describe this sequence. S1 confirms the Signals tab shows tags and ratings.
